successors.name: Roman Empire
successors.text: their territory 'annexed' with the suppression of the Pannonian revolts of 11-8 BC, then divided among several provinces; 'the territory they dominated covered much of what later became Moesia…

ledger.x: c. 279/278: the Scordisci settle at the Sava-Danube confluence. They 'settled at the confluence of the Sava and the Danube under a leader named Bathanatus' after the Delphi campaign, 'settling there about 279/278 BC and taking the name Scordisci'.
2nd century BC: the Scordisci reach their greatest extent.
14: Tiberius's punitive campaign: in 14 BC Tiberius led a punitive campaign against them, after which they appear only as allies of Rome; the last Scordiscan raid on Macedonia is 16 BC.
8: the client relation ends in annexation, 'With the suppression of the Pannonian revolts of 11-8 BC their territory was annexed'.

wars.name: Roman campaign against the Dalmatians and the Scordisci
wars.outcome: 'In 156 BC the consuls Lucius Lentulus and Gaius Marcius defeated the Dalmatians and the Scordisci'; no land changed hands on the page.

wars.name: Scordisci raids on Roman Macedonia
wars.outcome: From about 120 BC 'frequent raids into the province of Macedonia'; they killed the praetor Sextus Pompeius in 119, beat Romans in 141, were beaten by Marcus Annius (119), Minucius Rufus (110-109) and Scipio Asiaticus (84); the last raid recorded is 16 BC…

wars.name: Roman conquest of the Scordisci
wars.outcome: Tiberius's punitive campaign of 14 BC left them allies of Rome; the Pannonian revolts of 11-8 BC ended with the territory annexed.

certainty.note: The page names rivers and neighbours (the Taurisci to the north-west, Illyrian mountain peoples to the south) but no frontier; the page calls the society 'heterarchical ... without marked hierarchy or central authority', so the drawn shape…
